review_notes:
I read the whole file from the supplied text (lines 1–82). I did not open any related sources and I did not run Lean.

Almost every proof is a one-line `simp` call with two floor/ceil characterisation lemmas, such as `simp [floor_lt, le_floor]`. The lemmas differ in which characterisations they use and in which nonnegativity hypotheses they take. The `Nat` versions also differ in their side conditions.

The only longer proof is `Nat.cast_mem_Ioc_iff`. It splits on `0 ≤ b` and then calls `grind`. Nothing like it is repeated elsewhere in the file. The deprecated alias `cast_mem_Ioc_iff'` is a thin wrapper.

I found no nontrivial reasoning repeated across two or more proofs. The rubric calls short calculations and routine unfolding insufficient, so a shared lemma would not make the file clearer or easier to maintain.

My remaining uncertainty is that I did not look elsewhere in the library for similar proofs.
